However, there's an ambiguity in what "happened before" means. If it refers to:
- When the play was written/performed: Yes, early 1600s is before 1986
- The chronological events depicted in the play: The play is a comedy set in a fictional timeframe, so this is unclear

The most reasonable interpretation is that the play (as a work) predates the imaging of the scarp, which is factually correct.

The claim can be verified using the provided passages. Passage [1] confirms that "All's Well That Ends Well" is one of three Shakespearean problem plays written between the late 1590s and the first years of the 17th century. Passage [7] identifies that Rousillon Rupes, a scarp on Titania, is named after a character from "All's Well That Ends Well" and was first imaged by Voyager 2 in January 1986. Since the play was written in the early 1600s and the scarp was first imaged in 1986, the play chronologically "happened before" (predates) the imaging of the scarp. The claim is verified as factually correct.
When was "All's Well That Ends Well" written, and when was Rousillon Rupes on Titania first imaged by Voyager 2?

The claim is verified as factually correct. "All's Well That Ends Well" is one of three Shakespearean problem plays written between the late 1590s and early 1600s (specifically 1604-1605 according to Passage [3]). Rousillon Rupes, a scarp on the moon Titania named after a character from this play, was first imaged by Voyager 2 in January 1986 (Passage [1]). Since the play was written centuries before the scarp was imaged, the play did indeed "happen before" the imaging of the scarp.
